title: Long-term storage of Zymoseptoria tritici on silica gel
author: Rodney Pettway
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.s2regd6

steps.title: Sterilize silica gel powder
steps.instruction: Dry heat sterilize a fresh batch of silica gel powder in an oven at 190 C for 3-4 hours.

substeps.instruction: Optional: Mix 1 part indicator silica gel with 9 parts silica gel (10% indicator gel by volume).
Place silica gel in a shallow layer in a baking tray or glass beaker.
Transfer dried, sterilized silica gel to a sterile glass beaker.
Cover the beaker tightly with foil and allow to cool to room temperature for approximately 30 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare screw top vials
steps.instruction: Sterilize 2 ml screw top vials in an autoclave and ensure they are absolutely dry before use.

steps.title: Fill vials with silica gel
steps.instruction: Fill the sterilized vials with silica gel and label them.

substeps.instruction: Use a funnel to add silica gel to within one centimeter of the bottom thread on the screw top vial.

steps.title: Inoculate silica gel with spores
steps.instruction: Add a fresh spore or yeast cell solution to the silica gel vials and disperse the sample.

substeps.instruction: Add 150 microliters of the solution to the vial.
With the top loosely screwed down, shake the vial and rap with a finger to disperse spores over the silica gel (maximum 15 seconds).
Screw the top down as tight as possible.
Transfer immediately to an ice bucket and keep there until all isolates are transferred.

steps.title: Store isolates
steps.instruction: Store the labeled vials in a storage box at -80 degrees Celsius.

substeps.instruction: Optional: Place storage boxes in a container with approximately two cups of fresh silica gel in the bottom and label the outside of the container.

steps.title: Recover isolates from storage
steps.instruction: Recover the fungus by transferring the spore clump from the tube onto an agar plate.

substeps.instruction: Spread the clump on the plate to obtain fresh colonies.
Check indicator crystals in the tube every time it is opened; if all crystals indicate humidity, prepare a fresh long-term storage vial for that isolate.
